description: This challenge focuses on harmonizing NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS active fire hotspot data into a unified Burning Activity Calendar. The application will integrate both datasets to help users explore and analyze fire activity worldwide through interactive maps, historical charts, and seasonal comparisons. It aims to identify fire patterns, track changes over time, and make satellite data more accessible for researchers and decision-makers.
summary:
**FireSync** is an interactive web platform that harmonizes fire hotspot detections from NASA's MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) satellite sensors into one consistent record. The two sensors detect fires at different resolutions, so counts and trends can't be compared directly. FireSync matches detections that fall within about 1 km and 12 hours of each other and merges them into a single harmonized hotspot count that avoids double-counting.

Users explore the results on a 3D globe showing hotspots worldwide. They click any country to select it, then choose a date range. The sidebar offers a burning activity calendar, historical analytics, country comparison, auto-generated fire stories, environmental context, an AI fire assistant and CSV export.

This matters because wildfires affect air quality, ecosystems, climate and communities. A harmonized view gives researchers, journalists and the public clearer, more comparable fire information across sensors, countries and years, and it makes satellite data easier for non-experts to understand.

This prototype currently uses simulated data modeled on MODIS and VIIRS behavior, and it is designed to be connected to real NASA FIRMS detections.
details:
Project Details

What it does and how it works

FireSync combines active-fire detections from two NASA sensors: MODIS (1 km pixels, since 2000) and VIIRS (375 m pixels, since 2012). Because the sensors differ in resolution, they report different counts for the same fires. FireSync treats detections within about 1 km and 12 hours of each other as one fire. It counts them once (harmonized total = VIIRS + MODIS − matched pairs) and cross-calibrates MODIS fire radiative power (FRP) to VIIRS.

Users start on a rotating 3D globe with hotspots plotted worldwide. They click a country, pick a date range, and the sidebar updates with:

  • Harmonization: sensor counts, matched pairs and the harmonized total.
  • Burning Activity Calendar: a daily heatmap for each year.
  • Historical Analytics: yearly trends from 2016 to 2025.
  • Country Comparison: totals and hotspots per 10,000 km².
  • Fire Storytelling: an auto-written narrative of the season.
  • Environmental Context: vegetation type, an estimated CO₂ release and a smoke-exposure level.
  • AI Fire Assistant: answers questions about the selected data.
  • CSV Export: daily counts to copy into a spreadsheet.

Benefits and intended impact

Researchers get fire trends that stay comparable across sensors and years. Journalists, educators and communities get an easy, visual way to see where and when fires burn. The goal is to make satellite fire data understandable to non-experts and to support wildfire awareness, smoke-exposure awareness and climate discussion.

Tools and technologies

HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript, with the HTML5 Canvas API drawing the globe from custom orthographic-projection code and SVG for the charts. There are no external libraries and no server. The prototype was developed with the help of an AI assistant (Claude).

Creativity

Instead of a flat map, the globe lets users explore fire activity worldwide and click straight into a country. Harmonization is shown visually through sensor toggles, so users can see where the two sensors agree. The storytelling feature turns numbers into a readable narrative.

Factors considered

  • Accuracy: matching detections across sensors without double-counting fires.
    • The current data is simulated to mimic MODIS and VIIRS behavior.
    • Country selection uses approximate boxes rather than true borders.
    • The AI assistant is rule-based.

Next steps: connect to real NASA FIRMS data, add true country borders, and connect the assistant to a live AI model.
